original_value: Recognition systems using multimodal biometrics attracts attention because they improve recognition efficiency and high‐security level compared to the unimodal biometrics system. In this study, the authors present a secure multimodal biometrics recognition system based on the deep learning method that uses convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The authors propose two multimodal architectures using the finger knuckle print (FKP) and the finger vein (FV) biometrics with different levels of fusion: the features level fusion and scores level fusion. The features extraction for FKP and FV are performed using transfer learning CNN architectures: AlexNet, VGG16, and ResNet50. The key step aims to select separate features descriptors from each unimodal biometrics modality. After that, the authors combine them using the proposed fusion approaches were support vector machine or Softmax applies as classifiers to increase the proposed system security. The efficiency of the proposed algorithms is tested using publicly available biometrics databases. The experimental results show that the proposed fusion architectures achieve an accuracy of 99.89% and an equal error rate of 0.05%. The obtained results indicate that the biometrics recognition system using deep learning is secure, robust, and reliable.

result.paraphrase: Multimodal biometric recognition systems have drawn attention because they offer better recognition efficiency and a higher security level than unimodal biometric systems. In this study, the authors introduce a secure multimodal biometric recognition system based on deep learning with convolutional neural networks (CNNs). They propose two multimodal architectures that combine finger knuckle print (FKP) and finger vein (FV) biometrics at different fusion stages: feature-level fusion and score-level fusion. Feature extraction for FKP and FV is carried out through transfer-learning CNN architectures, namely AlexNet, VGG16, and ResNet50. The main step is to obtain separate feature descriptors from each unimodal biometric modality. These features are then merged using the proposed fusion methods, while support vector machine or Softmax is used as the classifier to improve system security. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithms is evaluated on publicly available biometric databases. Experimental results show that the fusion architectures achieve 99.89% accuracy and an equal error rate of 0.05%. These results indicate that the deep-learning-based biometric recognition system is secure, robust, and reliable.
